ops.title: Phase 2's incremental repair was abandoned for a clean-slate core redesign
ops.body:
**Decision, 2026-07-29.** The remediation plan's Phase 2 — repair the handshake budgets, settlement,
the disabled-agent gap and the client incrementally — was **abandoned mid-flight** and replaced with
a clean-slate structural design of the lifecycle core. Nothing from Phase 2 landed on `main`, which
stays at `0e60747`.

## Why

The owner's standing mandate was *"a lot of this seems to be stemming from a ton of
overcomplication/over-engineering bandaids; lets get back to basics, use what we've learned to
implement this clean, once, with the right abstractions"*. Phase 2 was violating it, and three lanes
proved it independently:

| Lane | What happened | What it says structurally |
|---|---|---|
| A2 settlement | Failed adversarial review **three times** (two implementations + the design). Each revision grew: an AST guard with mutation fixtures, "fenced supersession", a "counting law" with `provenGen`/`anyProofYet` | The duty is *reachable* from four owners — `Manager`, `PreparedChild`, `Reaper`, `FileStore` — so every fix adds a guard against the other three |
| A1 budgets | Landed, but had to **double `defaultHandshakeTimeout` 10s→20s** to make containment arithmetic fit, and found a **sixth** restated budget at `daemon/runtime.go:29` outside its scope | Bounds are *restated*, not inherited |
| B4 client | Premise refuted: `ServiceClient` requires readiness-subscription authority (`wire/runtime_bind.go:397-398`) that **no consumer's business client can hold** — `trust.UnprotectedRole` is structurally forbidden it (`trust/policy.go:222-231`). All three remedies offered were workarounds | One name for two things |

The owner's verdict on being shown those three options: *"restructure everything from scratch in a
way that makes sense dont work around current broken shit."*

## The generalization

All four symptoms are one defect: **the types do not carry the invariant, so discipline has to.**
Patching adds discipline, which is why every revision grew instead of shrinking. The design bar that
follows from it — and the bar the redesign is judged against:

> If an invariant needs a guard, a lint, a convention, a doc comment, or an AST test to hold, the
> design is wrong. Redesign until the invariant is a property of the types.

The A2 design needing a `go/ast` walker to forbid method calls outside one function is the tell, not
the fix.

## What survives — the evidence, not the structures

Phase 2's lanes ran to completion and their output is preserved at
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-yasyf-Code-daemonkit/phase2/`. It feeds the redesign as *evidence*, never
as a starting shape. The load-bearing findings:

- A **sixth** restated handshake budget: `trustProbeTimeout` at `daemon/runtime.go:29`.
- `DefaultReapSettlement`'s real cost is **13ms mean / 18.7ms max** against a 2s deadline — it is a
  deadline for the pathological case, not a cost.
- The long-cited "a trivial verifier run measures 1.78-2.69s" is **host fork/exec latency under
  load, not daemonkit's cost**: a raw two-line shell script measured 1.77s-31.76s on the same box.
  The defect it was used to justify is still real and still arithmetic; the magnitude must not size
  a constant.
- `FileStore.Remove` **returns nil without removing** when another generation holds the claim
  (`proc/filestore.go:792-799`).
- `FileStore.BeginReap` rejects a different-generation claim (`:912-919`), so a claimant that dies
  **orphans the record forever**.
- **bbolt's fsync commit is uninterruptible** — a context check before it bounds nothing, so any
  design that puts terminalization downstream of a synchronous store call can wedge unboundedly.
- `ServiceClient`'s lifecycle-lane vs business-lane split is **authorization-enforced**, not
  accidental — and it is the second half of why it was never adopted, alongside the chronology.

## The replacement

Four independent clean-slate designs (invariant-first, consumer-first, failure-first,
ownership-first), three judges on diverse lenses (structural / failure-replay / adoptability), one
synthesis. A judge panel rather than one-attempt-iterated, precisely because one-attempt-iterated is
what failed three times on A2. Targets: core types under ~200 lines of Go, spec under ~1,500 lines.
